title: Service Contracts: how many contracts may one customer hold?
content:
## Rule
Under the Aurelia Hanse Line (AHL) Service Contracts product, a customer may hold several service contracts, one per trade lane. There is no cap on the number of lanes on which one customer may hold a contract.

This clause settles only that a customer may spread its contracts over as many lanes as it wishes, one contract to a lane. How the contracts held on different lanes are aggregated with one another is not decided by this clause but by the portfolio aggregation rule of Service Contracts.

## In short
| Question | Answer under this clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of contracts or lanes per customer? | No cap on the number of lanes. |
| How many contracts per trade lane? | One per trade lane. |

## Points of judgement
**A customer already holds Service Contracts on three lanes and asks about a contract on a fourth lane. Does the number of lanes it already holds stand in the way?** No. The number of lanes is not capped, so holding three lanes does not by itself prevent a contract on a fourth.

**Does the clause allow two contracts on one lane?** The clause provides for one contract per trade lane.
